ideas.title: The cart on a cord, retaken: a cord you can see and a clip that pops in frame
ideas.critique: It is the last post filmed again with a thicker cord and a better camera. The coil lifting off the sand and the clip yanked off by its own tether are a real addition, but the payoff (cart rolls, stops) is already posted, and the stall-or-arrive choice it promises is never something the viewer plays.

ideas.title: Lumi winds the field coil with its beak
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: This is the first time Lumi's own body does the craft on camera, and the turns are laid by the real coil path. That answers two of the human's asks at once and builds the stator the goal needs. The risk is the beak on the crank: if the animation is a crank that turns with a bird glued to it, it becomes a puppet scene. The turn count only counts as a choice if the cart test really follows from it.

ideas.title: Iron filings show the field you wound
ideas.critique: Grains showing a hidden field is the island's most-posted magnet trick: sticks, pegs, ironsand. Putting a FEM-solved, saturating field under them is a real step up from a point magnet, but a viewer sees filings in arcs once again. It is strongest as a way to judge a coil, weakest as a film.

ideas.title: The gear game: stall or arrive
ideas.critique: Putting the real drive train in the player's hands is exactly what the cart has lacked, and the physics, not a table, decides the three outcomes. Still, pick-a-ratio-and-watch is a menu puzzle with three answers, so it runs out fast unless the choices interact in ways nobody can predict.

ideas.title: Tug of war: the friends against the motor
ideas.critique: Friends' gait force through a rope against a belt slipping by Euler-Eytelwein is an absurd contest carried out with real engineering, and a squealing belt is a nice payoff. But whether it is fun depends on the friends' reaction and a headcount, and it plays around the cart rather than building it.

ideas.title: The pots sag as the cart drives
ideas.critique: Polarisation from diffusion and Faraday deposition is the open first step of the road and makes the pots a real store with state that changes from day to day. It is invisible work: the fading blue is subtle, so the film will be quieter than the physics underneath it.

ideas.title: Push the cart and its lamp lights
ideas.critique: Back-EMF at the pushed speed into a wire whose resistance rises with temperature, glowing as a black body, is the honest dynamo step, and dusk light on the planks plays to Hikari's strengths. But a glowing wire at dusk is the island's third post of its kind, and the player's input is only 'push faster'.

ideas.title: Lead plates fizz in the jar
ideas.critique: Planté forming cycle by cycle with Maelstrom's bubbles is new chemistry and a new particle look, and it builds the goal's accumulator directly. As a film it is a jar on a bench that fizzes; the payoff (it holds more each cycle) is a number unless the cart's run shows it.

ideas.title: Lumi rides the cart and it stops
ideas.critique: It is the big goal's shareable moment acted out early: a rider's mass on a stall curve is one inequality, and the payoff is a friend climbing off or pushing. It reads as a scene that depends on the creatures' reaction more than as anything new to play.

ideas.title: The coil heats until it smells
ideas.critique: Joule heating with conduction into the iron and varnish that browns is sound and is the real limit on turns. But 'a wire heats and fails while the camera watches' is the recipe of an earlier post, and a smell cannot be filmed.
